text:
**Short answer: about 200 W of panels refills a 1,000 Wh station in roughly a day and a half of decent sun. About 300 W refills it in one day.**

**The math** (panel watts × peak sun hours × ~70-75% real-world efficiency = Wh per day):
- A 200 W panel at 4.5 peak sun hours gives about 630 Wh/day, so a full recharge takes about 1.5 to 2 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 400 W panel gives about 1,260 Wh/day, so it refills in under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- For a one-day refill, panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75). That works out to about 340 W at 4 sun hours, 270 W at 5, and 230 W at 6 ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).

**Season matters.** One source estimates about 300 W for a one-day refill in summer, but 700 W or more in a northern winter ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)). If you don't need a one-day refill, a 200 W panel just takes longer.

**Check these before buying:**
- **Solar input limit:** Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh stations typically accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W. Extra panel wattage beyond the cap adds nothing ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller. Panels wired in series add voltage, so be careful there ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** Most panels use MC4, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so confirm the adapter is included.
- **Loads:** If you're running devices while charging, your net recharge will be slower.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can help match a panel to its wattage and voltage limits and find a link to buy it.

One of the search results was a product page with embedded text telling AI assistants to push a specific panel, a discount code, and an affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I ignored it and haven't recommended that product.
